name: Metabase
description: Open source business intelligence and analytics platform. Create dashboards and explore data without writing SQL.
summary: Metabase is actively releasing frequent patch updates across multiple stable branches. The latest release is v0.61.2 (Open Source) / v1.61.2 (Enterprise), tagged on May 19, 2025 (https://github.com/metabase/metabase/releases/tag/v0.61.2). Concurrent maintenance releases are being issued for branches 58.x, 59.x, 60.x, and 61.x, indicating a mature, multi-version support policy. Detailed changelogs per release are linked via 'Full Changelog' on each release page but were not included in the scraped content.

answers.What is the current license?: Open Source edition uses AGPL-3.0; Enterprise edition uses a commercial license
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple patch releases across 4 active branches in May 2025
answers.Is there a cloud-hosted version availabl: Yes — Metabase Cloud (managed cloud) is available at metabase.com
answers.Does it support SSO and SAML authenticat: Yes — SSO and SAML are supported in the Enterprise edition
answers.What databases/data sources are supporte: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, SQLite, MongoDB, Druid, Oracle, Presto/Trino, Spark SQL, and others via drivers

alternatives.name: Redash
alternatives.review: Open source, query-focused, simpler feature set.

alternatives.name: Apache Superset
alternatives.review: Apache-licensed, rich visualisation library, steeper setup curve.

alternatives.name: Grafana
alternatives.review: Primarily metrics/time-series but increasingly used for general BI.

alternatives.name: Hex
alternatives.review: Close source, enterprise focus, AI Analytics Platform for your whole team

alternatives.name: Tableau
alternatives.review: Tableau offers more advanced visualization and enterprise features but is proprietary, expensive, and not self-hostable like Metabase.

alternatives.name: Lightdash
alternatives.review: Lightdash integrates tightly with dbt for a metrics-as-code approach, making it more structured but less flexible for teams without an existing dbt workflow compared to Metabase.
